title: Typed settings from the environment
problem: Write load_settings(env), which turns environment variables into a typed, frozen Settings object and fails fast with one clear ConfigError when the configuration is wrong. The OAuth client secret must never appear in a repr or an error message.
requirements: DATABASE_URL and OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET are required; a missing or blank (whitespace-only) value is missing
If any are missing, raise ConfigError naming every missing variable in one message
PORT: optional, default 8000; must be a whole number from 1 to 65535
DEBUG: optional, default False; accepts true/false/1/0/yes/no in any case; anything else (including an empty value) is an error
LOG_LEVEL: optional, default INFO; case-insensitive, stored uppercase; must be DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR or CRITICAL
Strip surrounding whitespace from every value; invalid optional values raise ConfigError naming the variable
repr(settings) and every error message must not contain the secret
Read only the mapping you're given, never os.environ directly
contract: load_settings(env: Mapping[str, str]) -> Settings   # raises ConfigError. Settings(database_url: str, oauth_client_secret: str, port: int = 8000, debug: bool = False, log_level: str = "INFO") is a frozen dataclass.
expectedBehavior: load_settings({'DATABASE_URL': 'sqlite:///x.db', 'OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET': 's', 'PORT': '8080'}) returns Settings with port 8080, debug False, log_level 'INFO'; load_settings({}) raises ConfigError mentioning both DATABASE_URL and OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET.
edgeCases: Empty mapping: both required names in one error
DEBUG 'on' or 'maybe' is rejected rather than guessed
Values with surrounding spaces or a trailing newline (common in .env files and CI variables)
hints: Conceptual: environment variables are always strings (or absent). Your job is the boundary: check presence first, collecting every problem with the required values, then convert and validate each optional value, and only then build the object.

Specific: collect the missing required names in a list and raise once if it's non-empty. For the secret, look at the dataclasses field() options: one of them controls whether a field appears in the generated __repr__.

Implementation: env.get(NAME, default).strip(); for PORT check .isdigit() and the range before int(); for DEBUG lower() and compare against two sets of words; field(repr=False) on oauth_client_secret; never put the secret's value into an f-string error.
evaluation: Each error message says which variable is wrong and what is allowed
No silent fallback: an invalid value is an error, not the default
